CHIEF COMPLAINT
Post-operative follow-up after bilateral reduction mammoplasty

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
36-year-old female status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10-10-2020 presenting for post-operative follow-up. Patient reports feeling well overall and that her breasts are healing nicely. She denies fever, chills, nausea, and vomiting. She reports resolution of previously experienced back pain. Patient notes that PA Ruth Sanchez identified a lump under her left breast during an office visit in March, though patient has not detected this since that time and has been performing self-massage. Physician assessed this as likely scar tissue. Patient reports her scars have been bothersome and she has been applying scar gel daily. She notes that one scar in particular causes more discomfort due to higher tension.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, and vomiting. Denies current back pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty on 10-10-2020

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying summertime. Family is doing well.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Bilateral breast examination performed. Bilateral incisions well-healed with no erythema or signs of infection. One scar noted with slight widening and evidence of high tension. No palpable lumps, hard spots, or bumps noted. Overall excellent healing.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
36-year-old female status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty on 10-10-2020 with excellent post-operative healing. Bilateral scar tissue noted with one area of widening and high tension. Patient counseled that definitive treatment of scars would require surgical scar revision and re-closure, which patient declines at this time. Patient instructed to continue mederma scar gel twice daily and to continue massage of scar tissue. Follow-up appointment in 6 months for re-evaluation of scars. Surgical revision not recommended until at least one year post-operatively. Photographs obtained today for documentation. Return to clinic in 6 months.
